clue.text: Difficulty going on after Ascot tip in racing

indicators.note: after places the word on behind the anagram
racing suggests the letters are whirled around at speed, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A punter backs a tip for a horse at Ascot races and keeps betting on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficulty going' looks like a racing term about soft ground, but it means trouble passing stools.
explanation.definitionFit: Constipation is literally difficulty in moving the bowels, a euphemism of going to the toilet.

clue.text: Part of toilet cold on one's rear

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's reads as has, joining it to what follows
the stern is the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone sits on a cold toilet seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is the water tank above or behind a flushing lavatory bowl.

clue.text: Those fixing cars — Reliant's part turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top
part means only a portion of the run of words is used

explanation.surface: Mechanics repairing cars find a bit of a Reliant car flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' picks SRELIAN out of 'cars Reliant's' and 'turned up' reverses it. 'Those fixing cars' looks like the definition, but 'cars' supplies the S. A Reliant Robin is a British three-wheeler, famous for tipping over.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailers are workers who fix things in place with nails.

clue.text: Follows name and number over a line

parts.note: a tag is a name or label

indicators.note: over means the song sits on top of, enclosing, the following letters

parts.note: a number is a song in a show

explanation.surface: A singer's name and their song get written over a line of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts SONG around A and L, giving SALONG.
explanation.definitionFit: To tag along is an idiom for accompanying or trailing after someone, as a hanger-on.

clue.text: Missing royal standards round five English flags

indicators.note: round means the shortened word goes around the next letters
missing means the royal letter is absent from the word for standards

parts.note: pars are normal standards, as in up to par
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in Royal Navy
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Royal banners are missing, and flags of England are on show instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing' takes R from PARS to give PAS, and 'round' puts PAS around VE. 'flags' is not banners here; it is a verb meaning lays with flagstones.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag a path means to lay flagstones on it, which is the same as paving it.

clue.text: Screwing books up — possible complaint of typist working

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books
RSI, repetitive strain injury, is an ailment typists may suffer
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: An office scene: books piled up and a typist complaining about their wrists while working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses OT to TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsion is the act of twisting, which is what screwing something round does.

clue.text: Feeling that makes some cry? Pain regularly piercing

indicators.note: piercing means the picked letters go into the vegetable

parts.note: chopping an onion makes people weep

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of pain

explanation.surface: A sentiment so painful it brings tears, stabbing like regular pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that makes some cry' is not part of the definition: it describes the vegetable that the alternate letters pierce.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or belief, as in what someone feels about a matter.

clue.text: Early star with banker set out recklessly

indicators.note: recklessly suggests letters thrown about without care, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A city banker sets off recklessly alongside a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is only a link. The star is from early cinema, not from early in someone's career.
explanation.definitionFit: Buster Keaton was a celebrated comic actor of the silent film era.

clue.text: Economic recovery over? Drink round noon

parts.note: up means over, as in time is up

indicators.note: round means the drink surrounds the letter for noon

parts.note: a swig is a gulp of drink

explanation.surface: With the recession over, someone celebrates with a drink at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts SWIG around N, giving SWING.
explanation.definitionFit: An upswing is an upward trend, used in economics for growth after a slump.

clue.text: Turning over channel to catch series — set off for film

indicators.note: to catch means the reversed channel holds the series inside it
turning over means the channel's letters are read backwards

parts.note: ITV is a British television channel
ER is a hospital drama television series
to go is to set off

explanation.surface: Someone switches channels to watch a series before heading off to see a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' looks like the definition, since vertigo feels like spinning, but it is the reversal signal. ER is an American hospital drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is Hitchcock's 1958 thriller starring James Stewart.

clue.text: See 19
In that place (South America) for May?

parts.note: there means in that place

explanation.surface: Someone asks if, in that place, South America, people celebrate May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the month, but it is the surname of Theresa May, British prime minister 2016 to 2019; the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The former British prime minister May had the first name, so it can be given for her.

clue.text: Help on inclination of talent contracted by newspapers

indicators.note: contracted means the word for talent is shortened by its final letter

parts.note: skill is talent
the i and the FT (Financial Times) are two British newspapers

explanation.surface: A talented person is signed up by the newspapers to help with their inclinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' looks like a signing, but it cuts SKILL to SKIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski lift carries skiers up a slope, giving them help on an incline.

clue.text: Splits payments

definitions.meaning: regular sums paid to a landlord

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both tears in cloth and money paid for using a property.

clue.text: Ruling men replace head of banking with director

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: replace head of means the first letter of the following word is swapped out
with names what goes in place of that first letter

parts.note: finance is the business of banking

explanation.surface: A ruling says that staff should replace the head of banking with a new director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replace head of' and 'with' swap the F of FINANCE for D, giving DINANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative decree or official rule.

clue.text: Developing Aldi: Tesco put out

indicators.note: developing suggests the letters are changing into a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: As discount store Aldi develops, rival supermarket Tesco is put out.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldi and Tesco are supermarket chains in Britain. 'put out' looks like annoyed, but it means displaced, as a joint is.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislocate a shoulder is to put it out of its socket.

clue.text: Swaps one-time lover and makes a connection

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a rail traveller changes trains to make a connection

explanation.surface: Someone trades in a former partner and connects with someone new.
explanation.definitionFit: Exchanges are trades, giving one thing and getting another back.

clue.text: Jimmy Carr, with offshore banking, primarily fiddled

indicators.note: fiddled means the letters are messed about with, so rearranged
primarily takes the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Comedian Jimmy Carr is accused of fiddling his taxes using offshore banking.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy Carr is a British comedian whose offshore tax scheme made headlines in 2012. 'Jimmy' looks like his first name, but it is the definition, a burglar's bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A jimmy is a short crowbar used by burglars to force doors and windows.

clue.text: Building issue when housing Victorians?

indicators.note: housing means the word for when holds the anagram inside it

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: building means the letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A planning issue arises when Victorian houses are being built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorians' looks like nineteenth-century people, but they are from the Australian state of Victoria; the question mark marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: People from the state of Victoria are Australians, informally Aussies.

clue.text: Ladies' man, Tramp, in jumper

indicators.note: in means the setter goes inside the jumper

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper
Tramp is the setter, who refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A womaniser, a tramp, is pictured wearing a jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: Tramp is this puzzle's setter, so the word stands for ME. 'jumper' looks like a sweater, but it is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romeo is a man who chases women, after Shakespeare's lover.

clue.text: Let's take most of Harrison Ford's fantastic film

indicators.note: fantastic suggests wild fancy, so the letters are rearranged
most of means the last letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: the actor's surname; the 's is only surface

explanation.surface: A cinema-goer suggests seeing most of a great Harrison Ford film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims HARRISON to HARRISO, and 'fantastic' rearranges that with LETSTAKE and FORD. Fittingly, Harrison Ford stars in the film.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiders of the Lost Ark is the 1981 Spielberg adventure, the first Indiana Jones film.

clue.text: Rabbit's mother put to sleep

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
under means anaesthetised, as in a patient going under

explanation.surface: A pet rabbit's mother has had to be put down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' looks like the animal, but it is British slang for talking on and on; the 's reads as is.
explanation.definitionFit: To maunder is to talk in a rambling, aimless way, as does the slang verb.

clue.text: Something stirring by cheat's right pocket

indicators.note: right means the right-hand, final, letter of the word for a cheat

parts.note: a rouser is something that stirs people up

explanation.surface: A rabble-rouser stands beside a cheat who is pocketing the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' puts the two pieces side by side. 'pocket' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser money is British slang for pocketing it, often dishonestly.

clue.text: Stiff with or without female on top

definitions.text: Stiff with or without female on top

parts.words: Stiff with or without female on top
parts.note: the word meaning stiff still means stiff, or frosty, when F for female is put in front of it

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Stiff', and the clue adds that putting F (female) on top gives another word, frigid, that also means stiff or cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means unbending or inflexible, much the same as stiff.

clue.text: Old half of Victoria line starts to delay users getting Tube

indicators.note: line means the half-name lines, or encloses, the starting letters
half of takes the first four of the eight letters of the name
starts to takes the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Commuters on London's Victoria line underground are delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground, and the Victoria line one of its routes, but the definition is an anatomical tube.
explanation.definitionFit: An oviduct is the duct carrying eggs from an ovary, so a kind of tube in the body.

clue.text: Catching Boycott's return, nearly got it

indicators.note: return means the word for boycott is read backwards

parts.note: to boycott is to ban; the 's is only surface

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: bingo is the cry of someone who has got it

explanation.surface: Cricketer Geoffrey Boycott returns and nearly makes a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses BAN to NAB and 'nearly' cuts BINGO to BING. Geoffrey Boycott is a famous Yorkshire and England cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab is to catch or seize, so nabbing means catching.

clue.text: One improving in the morning, one coming last

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning
an ender is one who comes at the end

explanation.surface: Someone gets better in the mornings, but still finishes last.
explanation.definitionFit: An amender is a person who corrects or improves something, such as a text.

clue.text: Annoyed one preparing for TV

parts.note: cross means annoyed
a dresser prepares food, wounds, or an actor for the stage

explanation.surface: An irritated person gets ready to go on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'TV' looks like television, but here it is short for transvestite.
explanation.definitionFit: TV is an abbreviation of transvestite, a person wearing clothes of the opposite sex.
